title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.
key_points: Physical Intelligence's first generalist robot foundation model (π0, 'pi-zero'), late 2024.
A Vision-Language-Action model: vision + language in, continuous robot actions out.
Built on a pretrained vision-language model (PaliGemma) plus a flow-matching action head.
Trained on 10,000+ hours across 7 robot types and 68 tasks, transferring to new ones.
content_html: π0 ("pi-zero"), from the startup Physical Intelligence, is a vision-language-action (VLA) model meant to be a generalist policy for robot control: a single model that looks at the world, reads a natural-language instruction, and produces the low-level actions to carry it out across many different robots and tasks.
extra_html:
How it works

π0 builds on a pretrained vision-language model — PaliGemma, ~3B parameters — so it inherits broad visual and language understanding, then adds an action-generation mechanism based on flow matching to output continuous, high-frequency motor commands rather than discrete tokens. Its inputs are camera images, the robot's joint angles, and a language command; its output is a sequence of action chunks. It was pretrained on over 10,000 hours of data spanning seven robot configurations and 68 tasks, then shown folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries, and assembling boxes.

Why it matters

π0 brought the "foundation model" recipe — pretrain broadly, then adapt — to robotics, building on Google's RT-1/RT-2 line. Reusing a vision-language model as the backbone lets the policy benefit from internet-scale semantic knowledge, and flow-matching actions give the smooth, dexterous control that earlier token-based policies struggled with. It is a notable step toward general-purpose robots that follow plain-language instructions.
